text: 一个事实是，绝大部分男生，或者可以说全部男生，在恋爱中的策略采用的都是减分的方式。
en: A fact is that the vast majority of boys, or one could say all boys, adopt a point-deducting strategy in their relationships.

text: 而当分数减到一定地步了，男生觉得自己忍不了了，就会离开，从而在女生眼中看起来特别绝情。
en: And when the score has been deducted to a certain point, the boy feels he can no longer bear it and will leave, which makes him seem especially heartless in the girl's eyes.

text: 其实只是分减到底线了而已，所有男生都有个底线，区别在于底线不同罢了。
en: In truth it is merely that the score has dropped to the bottom line; every boy has a bottom line, the only difference being that the bottom lines differ.

text: 比如女孩子无理取闹，男生是会原谅，但是内心会减分。
en: For instance, when a girl acts unreasonably, the boy will forgive her, but inwardly he deducts points.

text: 次数越多分减少的越多。
en: The more often it happens, the more points are deducted.

text: 比如女孩子和其他男孩子走的过近，减分。
en: For instance, when a girl gets too close to other boys, points are deducted.

text: 比如吵架非要男孩子道歉，减分。
en: For instance, when an argument insists that the boy apologise, points are deducted.

text: 有无数种减分的方式。
en: There are countless ways to deduct points.

text: 区别就在于当女生心里不舒服或者生气的时候，会选择哭还有闹还有吵架，从而男生过来哄她，所以释放了她的情绪。
en: The difference is that when a girl feels upset or angry, she will choose to cry, to make a scene, or to argue, so that the boy comes to coax her, thereby releasing her emotions.

text: 而男生因为面子的原因不能选择这种方式来表达自己的不开心，而且又不能吵架，因为所有的男孩子都很厌烦吵架，不管是谁的错吵架以后都得他去哄女朋友。
en: Whereas boys, because of their pride, cannot choose this way to express their unhappiness, and moreover cannot argue, because all boys detest quarrelling; regardless of whose fault it is, after a row he must be the one to coax his girlfriend.

text: 所以男孩子想来想去也只能压在心里了，他们就会想算了吧，就这样，不吵架省的还闹心。
en: So boys, after turning it over in their minds, can only bottle it up inside; they think, let it go, just leave it, better not to quarrel and spare themselves the aggravation.

text: 所以很多男孩子会包容女孩子的作，但是本质不是因为包容，而是因为两害相权取其轻，不包容的话女孩子就更哭更闹更作，还不如最开始就包容呢。
en: So many boys tolerate a girl's fussing, but the essence is not tolerance; rather it is choosing the lesser of two evils—if he does not tolerate her, the girl will cry, make a scene, and fuss even more, so it is better to tolerate her from the start.

text: 但这一切的一切，男生觉得算了吧就这样的事情，或者被男生忍下来的事情，都会是减分项。
en: Yet all of this—the things boys think 'let it go, just leave it', or the things boys swallow and endure—all count as point deductions.

text: 区别在于有的减分多有的减分少，而且每个人的底线不一样。
en: The difference is that some deduct more points and some fewer, and everyone's bottom line is different.

text: 但是大部分男生都会这样，等到减的分数少于底线了，男孩子也就到了离开的时候了。
en: But most boys are like this: once the score falls below the bottom line, the boy has reached the time to leave.

text: 这就是真实而理性的男生啊。
en: This is the real and rational boy.

text: 有一次，和一个男生一起走。
en: Once, I was walking along with a boy.

text: 他替我拎东西，超市买了很多，很沉。
en: He carried things for me; we had bought a great deal at the supermarket and it was very heavy.

text: 他走到楼下，放下袋子，使劲甩着手感叹道：好累啊！
en: He walked downstairs, set the bags down, swung his hands hard and sighed: so tired!

text: 我闻言大吃一惊：你拎东西也会觉得累吗？
en: I was greatly taken aback at this: you get tired from carrying things too?

text: 他一副没好气的样子说：当然会了。
en: He said, looking rather put out: of course I do.

text: 啊，请不要笑我白痴。
en: Ah, please do not laugh at me for being an idiot.

text: 我真的是活到接近这个岁数了，才第一次知道原来男人拎东西也会累的。
en: It was only when I had lived to nearly this age that I first learned that men get tired from carrying things too.

text: 这是因为父亲这样的男人，带给我带来的错觉。
en: This is because a man like my father gave me a false impression.

text: 我从小到大，从来没有听他抱怨过累的，无论他工作多辛苦，无论他拎多么重的东西。
en: From childhood to now, I have never heard him complain of being tired, no matter how hard he worked, no matter how heavy the things he carried.

text: 导致我错以为，男人都是力大无穷的。
en: Which led me wrongly to believe that men are all infinitely strong.

text: 记忆中的父亲还从来不吃好吃的，总是把零食、水果，美味的东西都让给我们，导致我曾以为男人都是不喜欢吃东西的。
en: In my memory, my father also never ate the nice food, always giving us the snacks, fruit, and delicacies, which led me once to think that men simply do not care for eating.

text: 关于男人的误会还有很多，后来我才知道：原来男人也是会没有安全感的，男人也需要赞美和鼓励的，男人有时候也很脆弱的，他们也会受到伤害的，也会有害怕的时候，也需要温暖和安慰的，也害怕被异性玩弄感情，赚钱也不会更容易…
en: There are many more misunderstandings about men; only later did I come to learn: it turns out men too can lack a sense of security, men too need praise and encouragement, men are sometimes quite fragile too, they too can be hurt, they too have moments of fear, they too need warmth and comfort, they too fear having their feelings toyed with by the opposite sex, and earning money is no easier for them…

text: 才知道，原来眼前的男人，虽然比我们高，比我们壮，比我们有力气。
en: Only then did I learn that the man before my eyes, though taller than us, sturdier than us, stronger than us,

text: 可是，他们并不是超人，他们心里也仍然住着一个小男孩。
en: Yet they are not Superman, and in their hearts there still lives a little boy.

text: 需要我们温柔去对待。
en: They need to be treated with gentleness.

text: 女朋友很喜欢DR钻戒，我觉得钻戒不保值，我该买给她吗？
en: My girlfriend really likes DR diamond rings, but I think diamond rings do not hold their value; should I buy her one?

text: 有一条，我不知道我要不要写啊，算了，反正都是写给我自己看的。
en: There is one thing—I do not know whether I ought to write it; oh well, anyway it is all written for me to read myself.

text: 很多人其实是没有爱的，他需要的只是满足他各种各样的需求。
en: Many people actually have no love; what they need is only to satisfy their various demands.

text: 这句话的信息量是很大的，几乎概括了所有的博弈。
en: The information carried in this sentence is considerable; it almost summarises every game of strategy.

text: 男性最真实的一面就是，他一定知道他娶你是为了什么，但是女性的话就不一定了。
en: The truest side of men is this: he definitely knows why he married you, but for women it is not necessarily so.

text: 举一个例子吧，有很多女人的婚姻，包括我妈，她都会有这样一个想法。
en: Let me give an example: many women's marriages, including my mother's, share this kind of thinking.

text: 就是“我不图钱，不图利，就图当初对我的好，可是婚后他一下子就变了，连那点好都没有了，最后连我自己都不知道我到底图个啥。
en: Which is: “I want neither money nor gain; I only wanted the kindness shown to me at the start, but after marriage he changed all at once, and not even that bit of kindness remained; in the end I no longer even know what on earth it was I wanted.

text: 我个人其实很恐惧一句话，叫“鱼上钩了谁还放饵。
en: Personally I actually dread one phrase, which goes: “Once the fish is on the hook, who would still put out the bait.

text: ”这句话的本质逻辑就是，我不想对你好，我只想要到我要的利益，利益到了，那份好就没了，这份好只是短暂虚晃的一枪。
en: ”The essential logic of this phrase is that I do not want to be good to you; I only want to get the benefit I am after. Once the benefit is obtained, that goodness is gone—that goodness was merely a brief, feigned thrust.

text: 这跟“花钱哄女孩子开心，来骗女方身子，睡到了就翻脸”，本质上一个逻辑。
en: This is essentially the same logic as 'spending money to cheer a girl up, so as to deceive the woman out of her body, and turning hostile the moment she has been slept with'.

text: 商业街，万圣节活动。
en: Shopping street, Halloween event.

text: 把尖顶的巫师帽带在头上，手舞足蹈的像个逗逼。
en: With a pointed wizard's hat on the head, dancing and waving about like a clown.

text: 姑娘说，你怎么这个德行。
en: The girl said, what on earth is with that behaviour of yours.

text: 书店里，路过幼儿区。
en: In the bookshop, passing through the children's section.

text: 认真的看呆萌的儿童读本，忍俊不禁的像个傻逼。
en: Reading the adorable children's picture books with real concentration, unable to stifle a laugh, like an idiot.

text: 姑娘说，你能不能成熟点儿。
en: The girl said, can you be a bit more mature.

text: 逛超市，看到蛋糕专柜。
en: Browsing the supermarket, coming to the cake counter.

text: 对着法式布朗尼和芝士蛋糕流口水，星星眼。
en: Drooling over the French brownie and cheesecake, eyes shining like stars.

text: 姑娘说，你居然喜欢吃这个。
en: The girl said, you actually like eating this.

text: 于是后来我和姑娘在一起的时候，都不做这些事情了。
en: So afterwards, when I was with the girl, I stopped doing any of these things.

text: 但是再后来，我觉得不对啊：世界上有些东西不是极端的，非黑即白的。
en: But still later, I felt something was wrong: some things in the world are not extreme, not black-and-white.

text: 世界上很多事情都是没什么卵蛋联系，这些所谓的“联系”都是人为主观臆造的。
en: Many things in the world have no real connection whatsoever; these so-called 'connections' are all subjectively invented by people.

text: 我的确喜欢看儿童读本，但我也很喜欢看数学和社科类的书。
en: It is true that I like reading children's books, but I also very much like reading mathematics and social-science books.

text: 我也的确喜欢吃甜食和零食，但这不妨碍我边在街边吃烤串，边拎着啤酒瓶子吨吨吨吨。
en: It is also true that I like eating sweets and snacks, but that does not stop me from eating skewers by the roadside while guzzling from a beer bottle.

text: 所以你想看男生真实的一面，其实很简单。
en: So if you want to see a boy's true side, it is actually quite simple.

text: 让他放轻松，觉得你是一个可以信任的人。
en: Let him relax and feel that you are someone he can trust.

text: 不要因为某些“性别政治正确”嘲笑他，并且该犯傻的时候和他一起犯傻，这就好了。
en: Do not mock him because of certain 'gender political correctness', and when it is time to act silly, act silly together with him—that is all.

text: 但是这又很难。
en: But this too is difficult.

text: 你说这完全是姑娘的错吗？
en: Would you say this is entirely the girl's fault?

text: 我感觉不是。
en: I do not think so.

text: 只能说这个社会“政治正确”的风气愈演愈烈。
en: One can only say that the climate of 'political correctness' in this society grows ever more intense.

text: 人们都喜欢用片面的“政治正确”去衡量人，而从来不会从全面的角度，去考察这个人到底是怎样的一个真实的人。
en: People all like to measure a person by one-sided 'political correctness', yet never examine from a comprehensive angle what sort of real person this individual actually is.

text: 譬如说姑娘，倘若你没有化妆品，不喜欢逛街——那你就是“政治错误”。
en: Take the girl, for instance: if you have no cosmetics and do not like shopping—then you are 'politically incorrect'.

text: 再譬如说男人，倘若你没有衣冠楚楚，不喜欢体育运动——那你也是“政治错误”。
en: Take the man, for instance: if you are not immaculately dressed and do not like sport—then you too are 'politically incorrect'.

text: 对于“政治错误”的，我想是要被打倒在地，并踏上一万只脚的。
en: As for those who are 'politically incorrect', I imagine they are to be struck to the ground and trampled by ten thousand feet.

text: 但问题的关键是：化妆品，逛街，衣冠楚楚和体育运动，这些片面的东西几乎是无法判定一个人的性格和品德的。
en: But the key point is this: cosmetics, shopping, being immaculately dressed, and sport—these one-sided things can scarcely determine a person's character or virtue.

text: 而现实是，所有人都死揪着那几个“政治正确”的点不放，而完美的忽略了每个人的灵魂各有不同。
en: Yet the reality is that everyone clings stubbornly to those few points of 'political correctness' and perfectly ignores that every person's soul is different.

text: 所以你说，男生的真正一面是什么呢？
en: So tell me, what is a boy's true side?

text: 每个人都是不一样的。
en: Every person is different.

text: 他可能喜欢和小孩子在一起玩耍，也可能喜欢安静的读一本晦涩的书籍；他可能习惯于凡事都自己一个人粗暴的解决，也可能习惯于在团队中默不作声；他可能对于性这方面的要求很渴望，也可能对这个东西不是很需求。
en: He may like to play with small children, or he may like to read a recondite book in quiet; he may be used to solving everything himself, roughly and alone, or he may be used to staying silent within a team; he may have a strong craving for sex, or he may not care much for it.

text: 你看吧。
en: You see.

text: 他很多时候都坦坦荡荡，或有心无意的展示给你看了。
en: Much of the time he is open and aboveboard, or shows it to you intentionally or unintentionally.

text: 只不过更多的时候，这些却被冠以“幼稚”，“木讷”，“专横”，“巨婴”，“直男”，“娘炮”…
en: It is just that more often, these are labelled 'childish', 'inarticulate', 'domineering', 'man-child', 'straight man', 'effeminate'…

text: 诸如此类的负面标签罢了。
en: Merely negative labels of that sort.
